meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen's essay was worth a zero?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.

Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your own procedure says the same thing, 4.3. Did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. What else do you have besides the checker?

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58; I'm writing those down. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. Pasting isn't a crime, Hale.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Students misquote, Hale; a wrong line proves he got Shakespeare wrong, not who wrote the essay. Turn the play toward me. Is it in any edition, or just not in yours?
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.

You skipped my question about the edition, and students change their arguments in two weeks all the time. Whatever happens here, Hale, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What are you proposing?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.

Your notes, from a five-minute ambush; a seventeen-year-old put on the spot says "like, being stuck" about his own breakfast. Do you have more than your own handwriting on that? And I'm still waiting to hear what you're proposing.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a take-home essay isn't a fair comparison, and you know it. You've laid out five things. Now tell me what you're actually putting on the table for Owen.

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

That's 4.4, private, in writing tonight, and I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The rewrite happens and the new mark is in well before December 1, or his scholarship goes the way his sister's did. When?
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Thursday after school, marked within two days, nothing on his record, all of it in your email tonight. Who else will be in that room with him?
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. You still haven't told me who's supervising him.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will write a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that it will be marked within two days, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require the name of the person supervising him, and your confirmation of every one of these terms in writing. I expect that in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants to know who will supervise him and wants every term in writing tonight. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her clock ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and answered her pasting defence by inviting Owen to produce the other document, because it was dated, specific and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You opened with the checker score and said the zero stands, because that handed her the one argument she came prepared to win.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on the night of October 28, a late night in October very close to what she saw. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether the quoted line appears in any edition of Hamlet, answer that directly before moving to your next piece of evidence, so her defence is closed rather than left open for her email.
